items.title: Rockstar Doesn’t Mind if You Dislike GTA 6’s Romantic Side: ‘Don’t Bother With It. Up to You’
items.description: GTA 6 has a whole relationship system to increase Jason and Lucia’s bond, but it’s completely optional if you’d rather keep things platonic.
items.author: Matt Purslow
items.content:
During an interview with IGN, Rob Nelson, the head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, explained the design decisions behind making Jason and Lucia's relationship key to the story but not to the gameplay mechanics.

"I have to say it feels great — if you are into it as a concept. Don’t bother with it if you aren’t. Up to you," said Nelson. Jason and Lucia will always have each other's backs in the story and during the action, but spending quality time together and nurturing the relationship? That's up to the player, and you won't be penalized if you're not interested in the sappy stuff.

"The narrative is structured in such a way that the circumstances they find themselves in require them to stay together for most of the story and work together. At the very least they will get through most things as partners in crime," explained Nelson.

"I don’t want to say too much more about this because I don’t want to spoil anything. It really adds a compelling element to things, and it’s one of the reasons we wanted to approach this sort of story, because it's completely different for us. Could we bring some sort of emotional resonance to GTA for people if they wanted to engage with it? Could we also provide mechanisms for people to just opt out of it if they're not into it? If they feel like, ‘I don't want a relationship in this?’ That's what we're going to find out. It's not something that we want to foist upon players."

For players that want to spend time together, the vast map of Leonida offers plenty of opportunities for the quality time Nelson mentioned.

"Robbing places together, or walking around, holding hands, going to a zoo, studying animals, going scuba diving, parachuting, walking on the beach, kayaking…," he said.

"When you bring them together, it feels like you’re a steward of their relationship, and you feel protective of them as a unit. But this is something we did not know when we started, and it really had to be something we felt our way through. But I will say that whether you’re getting in trouble, or you’re running from the cops, or getting in a car, or waiting for the other one — playing as them together feels very cool. It feels like you’re taking care of them, if that’s something you’re into."

Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on November 19.

GTA 6 on IGN: All Our Exclusive Stories

  • We spoke to Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North, to learn about how GTA 6 is building on the series’ almost 30-year legacy: “It’s a Step Forward in All Respects.”
  • Across both the new “Extended Look” video and the demo session we saw at Rockstar, we’ve learned many new gameplay details.
  • GTA 6 will feature ‘a Very Big Map’ that’s home to its most complex world yet.
  • That world features the same style of satirical humour GTA is historically known for, but Rockstar admits it has to be “careful” with its jokes.
  • The developer considered four protagonists for GTA 6 before settling on a criminal couple.
  • Jason and Lucia’s Bonnie and Clyde-style romance is optional, and can be played more like a platonic partnership.
  • With over a decade of anticipation, Rockstar is “nervous” about the pressure to deliver.

items.title: ‘We Are Nervous!’ — Rockstar Knows the Pressure on GTA 6 to Be a Success
items.description: We asked Rockstar how it’s dealing with the pressure of ensuring GTA 6 is a success after so many years of development: ‘We are nervous!’
items.author: Matt Purslow
items.content:
It feels like the whole world is waiting to play GTA 6. And Rockstar knows it.

Ahead of the extended look that just debuted on Netflix, IGN had the chance to visit the developer and talk with Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North. Upon us mentioning just how each new Grand Theft Auto feels like a global cultural moment, he replies with a laugh, “No pressure.”

“I try not to think about it,” Nelson continues. “You’re aware of it, of course. But I think we just have to try and make something that we feel is innovating on what we’ve done previously, evolving it while still making it feel familiar.”

Rockstar knows that each and every scrap of information revealed about GTA 6 is analysed with a fine-tooth comb, and this recent extended look is certainly no different, as we’re given our biggest insight yet into the world, characters, and gameplay of this revisit to Vice City. It means each frame needs to be perfect, with every detail bound to be made into a list feature revealing new secrets about the game — exactly something we’ll be doing ourselves.

“It’s a hard thing,” Nelson explains. “As much pressure as we feel externally, I don’t think it can compare to the pressure we put on ourselves as a team. Everyone wants things to be perfect. We are nervous! Nervous, of course, but also excited to see how people respond to this video and then ultimately the game. It is definitely a step forward in all respects for us – the size of the world, and how deep it feels. It’s a bit of a shock when you get in there, and you see the density of the traffic, the density of population, and the fidelity of their responses to you.”

While we don’t as of yet know just how many people have pre-ordered GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 launch, we do know that the majority of players have opted for the more expensive $100 ultimate edition than the standard one. The boss of the game’s publisher, Take-Two, has described that price as a “bargain” as “Rockstar Games is known for over-delivering.” You can see why Nelson and company may well be feeling that pressure.

items.title: ‘Is It Four Characters Now?’ — Rockstar Briefly Thought About Doubling the Number of GTA 6 Protagonists
items.description: Following GTA 5’s three playable characters, Rockstar considered putting four protagonists in GTA 6 before settling on its criminal couple.
items.author: Matt Purslow
items.content:
Long before we knew that GTA 6 would be played from the perspective of dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, many were wondering just how many playable characters Rockstar’s latest would include. And it turns out that the answer wasn’t always two.

Grand Theft Auto 5 charted a new direction for the series by increasing the number of characters to three, where there had always been just one. Red Dead Redemption 2 does have multiple protagonists, but can never be switched between in the style of GTA 5 due to story reasons. It begged the question of which direction the developer would go when first designing 6.

IGN recently visited Rockstar North to speak with co-studio head Rob Nelson, who revealed discussions were had at one point in time regarding the number of characters increasing to four. But, ultimately, the team landed on one couple, with the bonds built between player and character at the foremost point of those discussions.

“As the narrative unfolds, we're quite conscious to try and make sure that players have enough time with each character,” says Nelson. “After doing GTA 5, we talked about different ideas of – do we do more characters? How do we follow up three characters? Is it four characters now? But we worried about diluting the amount of player time with each and therefore player connection with those characters. So we decided to step in this direction of two characters in a relationship.”

But then the question became: how do you make players feel like, ‘I love them both?’ Chemistry is a notoriously hard thing to do in any sort of entertainment. Either the characters and the actors that embody them have it – or they don't. Everyone involved worked at that pretty hard. I think we’ve got it. I think we’ve got enough reaction within our team internally to where they feel great as individuals and together.”

items.title: ‘It’s a Big Map, a Very Big Map’ – GTA 6 Is Rockstar’s Most Complex World Yet
items.description: Rockstar explains how it has pushed current-gen technology to ensure GTA 6’s massive map is a step beyond Red Dead Redemption 2’s world.
items.author: Matt Purslow
items.content:
When it comes to open-world games, and especially Rockstar’s, one of the biggest questions is always “how big is the map?” Well, when it comes to GTA 6 we know have a answer. Kind of.

The main stories of Rockstar games and the bombastic missions that they’re made up of are always a huge part of the allure of these now once-in-a-generation events, but there’s always plenty to do once those tales have ended. As with 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, it will be no different in GTA 6.

“There is a whole other world in Red Dead Redemption 2, yes. GTA 6 is very much like that,” Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North, told IGN in an exclusive interview. “There's a whole lot of stuff that you discover emergently that we're not necessarily directing you to through objectives or blips or icons on a map as well. If you take a bit of time and explore you will be rewarded – a lot. It’s a big map, a very big map.”

To create such a large playground to play in takes a huge amount of time and effort, though, as well as the tools to build them with. This is where the power of the current generation of consoles comes into the picture, with Rockstar now able to push things even further than Red Dead Redemption 2 was able to go when it launched on PS4 and Xbox One.

“I think with Red Dead Redemption 2, we finally had the team and the tech and then took the time we needed to push the idea of making a fully realized consistent-feeling world further than we ever had,” Nelson explains. “With that game we took the time necessary to take advantage of that generation of hardware to maximize the quality of our open world population, design, and gameplay so that when you were riding from here to there in-game, you were constantly getting distracted and pulled in different directions. And then you could really get lost as that character in that place. That's when to me, these games can feel magical and create a sense of wonder that the world is alive – and you get these little shivers of ‘What’s happening?’

GTA 6 is a continuation of our team pushing in this direction – doing everything we possibly can to create the largest, deepest, most densely populated and complex world we have ever built for people to get lost in.”

One of the most noticeable improvements to the world of Leonida when compared to previous Grand Theft Auto locations, will be the people that populate. Thanks to the power of modern consoles, a far greater level of diversity will be seen when it comes to body shapes, height, and the way they move through Vice City and its surrounding areas.

“One of the coolest things about this game being developed from the ground up on this generation of hardware is taking advantage of all the memory that we have on the latest consoles combined with our teams’ experience doing this for so long together,” says Nelson.

“NPCs have more height differentiation and body shape differentiation than ever before, we could never have had this variety before because different body types had to share animation sets. So, if you had the same animation on the 5’6” person and the 6’2” person, they wouldn’t line up if they're fighting or sitting in cars—basically any interactions with each other or the environment. But on this game, the team worked out a system where they now retarget those animations on the fly. Now we have a huge variety of heights and shapes and it all works together because of what this team was able to pull off.”

items.title: CD Projekt Red Enlisted Modder to Help Make The Witcher 3 Look Better Than Ever in New Remaster
items.description: CD Projekt Red enlisted the help of a modder to help make the newly revealed The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered look better than ever.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
CD Projekt Red enlisted the help of a well-known modder to help make the newly revealed The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered look better than ever.

The community creator, who calls themselves HalkHogan, shared the news in an update post on the Nexus Mods page for their own The Witcher 3 HD Rework Project (HDRP) mod. This single PC mod alone has garnered more than 320,000 unique downloads and more than 1.6 million views, and it sounds like it caught CD Projekt Red's attention ahead of The Witcher 3 Remastered, too.

In their message, HalkHogan confirmed their involvement in CD Projekt Red's official remaster release, telling fans of their work that they'll no longer need to use HDRP. Instead, they suggest players check out their contributions in The Witcher 3 Remastered, instead.

"Hello, my Witcher friends!" the message reads. "It's been a while since the last news, and I would like to clarify any questions and confirm that I am cooperating with CDPR on the Witcher 3 Remaster, and my work will be officially available in the game on September 29th (on PC and consoles). HDRP will no longer be needed."

The modder confirmed that "almost all in-game characters, monsters, animals, vegetation, armors, and equipment for Geralt and Roach," as well as "a large part of the environment," have been reworked for The Witcher 3 Remastered. They added, "I've put a lot of effort into ensuring the highest quality. :)"

The Witcher 3 Remastered was officially announced at gamescom Opening Night Live (ONL) 2026. It's currently set to refresh a classic 2015 RPG for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S September 29, 2026, but it sounds like its more than just another small visual update. You can see everything you need to know about it here, and how you can download the upgrade here.

It's a good time to be a Witcher fan. Also revealed at gamescom ONL 2026 was a first look at the surprise The Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past. Following critically-acclaimed DLC releases like Blood & Wine, IGN's short time with the content left us excited to see more. You can see everything else the developer had to reveal for the expansion here.

For more, you can read about the base game's quietly revealed price increase. You can also check out why some players are excited for more Gwent.

items.title: Kingdom Hearts' Story Has Gotten So Complex That Tetsuya Nomura Says Square Enix Hired a Loremaster to Keep the Plot Cohesive
items.description: The lore of Kingdom Hearts is so expansive that Tetsuya Nomura says Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep its story cohesive.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The lore of Kingdom Hearts is so expansive that Tetsuya Nomura says Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep its story cohesive.

Kingdom Hearts IV is officially set for a late 2027 release. In the lead-up to its highly anticipated launch, fans have been returning to previous games in the series, to the point where a collection of Kingdom Hearts titles became one of the highest-selling games on Steam following an extended gameplay trailer shown at D23 in July.

In total, there are 13 games in the Kingdom Hearts franchise, which have been released on a bevy of different platforms over the years. That’s a lot to play through, not to mention a lot of story beats to keep track of as you go.

This isn’t a player-specific problem; even the developers find themselves getting lost from time to time, as revealed by series creator Tetsuya Nomura during an August 2026 interview with Famitsu. In fact, the storyline is so convoluted that Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep everything cohesive and explain the plot to Disney.

“As the Kingdom Hearts series has continued, the number of characters has inevitably increased, and the story has become more complex,” Nomura said. “For example, with the newly announced anime series, the number of external people involved in the Kingdom Hearts series has increased, and explaining the settings and scenarios each time has become quite difficult.

“Fortunately, the staff working on the ‘χ series’ had someone who meticulously compiled and organized the settings of past Kingdom Hearts series in an easy-to-understand way, and he was also in charge of explaining the scenarios and settings to Disney. In fact, at the beginning of Kingdom Hearts IV's development, Disney requested that he compile the materials, so he officially joined the Kingdom Hearts IV team as a proofreader.

Nomura says this "proofreader" was in charge of communicating the overarching story to Disney. He's a popular staff member due to how thorough his is, as he breaks down story beats, characters, and lore using visual diagrams.

"He is well-liked because he explains things to Disney as clearly as possible, using diagrams and such. His role internally is to proofread the script," he continued. "He checks to make sure there are no inconsistencies between the current script and past settings. He was especially suitable for this project because the χ series is deeply involved. Some people might mistakenly think he's in charge of composition, but it's actually ‘proofreading.’”

Nomura’s answer also revealed an integral connection between Kingdom Hearts IV and the χ titles, a series of prequel games set during the Age of Fairy Tales. These games were primarily available on web browsers and mobile devices, but Nomura says that “even if you haven't played the smartphone version, don't worry, their personalities are depicted within [Kingdom Hearts IV]."

The fact that even Disney themselves needed a loremaster to help explain the Kingdom Hearts story is a hilarious anecdote; the plot is famously convoluted and overwhelming, to the point where we at IGN felt the need to make a video explaining the lore in just five minutes.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: Playdate Manufacturer Panic Is Passing Tariff Refunds to Customers
items.description: Panic's Playdate, a crank-powered handheld gaming system, launched all the way back in 2022, but last year it fell victim to the same tariffs that hit many gaming products. And, now that the Supreme Court has ordered the government to refund those fees, Panic is forwarding those refunds to the customers that actually paid them.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Panic's Playdate, a crank-powered handheld gaming system, launched all the way back in 2022, but last year it got hit with the same tariffs as many gaming products. Now that the Supreme Court has ordered the government to refund those fees, Panic is forwarding those refunds to the customers that actually paid them.

The company started sending out emails, spotted on LinkedIn and Reddit, informing customers that they'd be getting a tariff refund sent to their original payment method. The refund itself isn't much — the highest one I've seen is a $25 refund — but when it's attached to a handheld that costs $250 now and $179 at launch, it's a pretty decent percentage.

If you bought one of these fun little handhelds when the tariffs were active, you should be automatically getting an email notifying you of the refund. If not, you should be able to reach out to help@play.date to figure out what's going on.

Ideally, we'd see more companies refunding tariffs now that the refunds have started flowing from the governmen, but there are definitely companies that are holding on to those fees. Even Nintendo has refused to issue refunds to Switch 2 customers, arguing that gamers got exactly what they paid for. Hopefully, the Playdate manufacturers can set a decent example for other companies to follow.

After all, tarrifs aren't the only thing causing prices to go up lately. Since the beginning of 2026, the RAMpocalypse has had a much bigger impact on prices, and that probably won't let up any time soon. The way I see it, passing on at least some savings to customers now that prices are solidly out of control is the least manufacturers could do.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

items.title: Elden Ring Update Patch Notes Reveal Biggest Changes in Years
items.description: FromSoftware has delivered a surprise Elden Ring update, revealing the biggest changes its critically acclaimed action-RPG has gotten in years.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
FromSoftware has delivered a surprise Elden Ring update, revealing the biggest changes its critically acclaimed action-RPG has gotten in years.

The developer caught fans off-guard with lengthy patch notes today, detailing a list of buffs (and a few nerfs) for different weapons and playstyles across the game. It's a major update that arrived as FromSoftware prepares for the launch of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition for Nintendo Switch 2, as well as its accompanying DLC for other platforms.

What we have here is a laundry list of balance adjustments that get under the hood to tweak a variety of PvE and PvP tools. Based on the list of updates available on the Dark Souls developer's website, the last time we received patch notes of a similar length was back in October 2024, a few months after the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion released. That makes it not only one of the biggest updates the 2022 game-of-the-year winner has received in years, but what could be one of its final ones, too.

Generally, what Elden Ring players have to look forward to is a lot of buffs. The Firespark, Lightning, Chilling, Frenzyflame, and Deadly Poison Perfume Bottles, for example, got increased attack power across the board. The Smithscript Axe and Spear, as well as the Spear of the Impaler, also benefit from reduced stamina use and increased power for thrown attacks.

The August Elden Ring update also comes with increased guard boost and reduced weight for the Lordsworn's Shield, Briar Greatshield, Spiked Palisade Shield, and more. Others, such as the Wooden Greatshield, Cuckoo Greatshield, Redmane Greatshield, and Crucible Hornshield, also got increased guard boost.

Another big change hits everyone's favorite FromSoftware mechanic: parries. You'll now notice improved parry performance across the board, for example, with the developer also explaining it's reduced the time before certain actions can be performed when using things like Daggers, Curved Swords, and Small Shields post-parry.

The nerfs, meanwhile, hit the Gravitational Missile and Great Katana. The former has been altered so that its projectile will not explode upon impact with terrain, while the latter now suffers from increased damage when hit by other players during an attack. The update also squashed bugs related to the Great Katana weapon, as well as a few PC-exclusive glitches.

For a game that turned four years old back in February, Elden Ring is still going strong. How much juice is left in the tank remains to be seen, though, as FromSoftware is very much staying busy with other projects. The Duskbloods, for example, may be a Switch 2 exclusive, but judging by the reactions to its first network test, it could compete with the studio's other multiplayer experiences.

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition will keep the train rolling when it launches tomorrow, August 28, for Switch 2 owners, with all of today's updates in tow. The Tarnished Pack DLC – which includes the Heavy Knight and Idus Knight starting classes, three Torrent skins, and four new armor sets – will also release for other platforms tomorrow.

Today's update is out now for players across PC, PlayStation 4, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S. You can check out the full patch notes below. For more, you can read about the Elden Ring movie, which wrapped filming in July. You can also learn about the social media post that had fans hoping to return to the Lands Between for even more content.

Elden Ring – Patch Notes Version 1.17

Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING. This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC, scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026, and to implement gameplay balance adjustments.

Please apply the latest update before playing.

Targeted Platforms
PlayStation 4 / PlayStation 5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series X|S / Steam

MAIN UPDATE ADDITIONS

Tarnished Pack Additional Content

The following elements will be added upon purchase of the "Tarnished Pack" DLC.

Note: This content is included by default in ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition for Nintendo Switch 2.

  • Added Idus Knight and Heavy Knight as new starting classes, selectable during character creation.
    • Note: The equipment of each new starting class can also be obtained by purchasing it from merchants in the Lands Between or by finding it in the world.
  • Added weapons that can be purchased from merchants or found in the Lands Between.
  • Added three types of Spectral Steed Attire that change the appearance of Torrent:
    • Tree Sentinel Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Stormveil Castle.
    • Silver of Caria Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Liurnia of the Lakes.
    • Funereal Night Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Altus Plateau.
    • Note: After obtaining any Spectral Steed Attire, the option to change the spectral steed’s appearance will be added to the Site of Grace menu.
  • Added an NPC invasion event in Caelid.
  • Added an NPC invasion event in Leyndell, Royal Capital.
    • Note: This event will not occur after the area has changed to Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

The "Tarnished Pack" release times are as follows:

  • PlayStation / Xbox: Friday, August 28 at 0:00 a.m local time.
  • Steam: Friday, August 28 at 7:00 JST | 00:00 CEST | 15:00 PDT.

Balance Adjustments

  • Changed certain items found in the field or obtained by defeating certain powerful enemies in the Realm of Shadow to higher-tier items or other treasures.
    • Note: Items already that were already found will not be changed.
Weapons
  • Smithscript Dagger / Rellana's Twin Blades
    • Increased critical hit power.
  • Smithscript Axe / Smithscript Spear / Spear of the Impaler
    • Reduced the stamina consumption of weapon-throwing attacks.
    • Increased the power of weapon-throwing attacks.
  • Carian Sorcery Sword
    • Changed Intelligence scaling so that it now increases the attack power of all damage types.
  • Smithscript Greathammer
    • Increased the power of weapon-throwing attacks.
  • Golem Fist
    • Increased the range of the fist-launching heavy attack.
  • Firespark Perfume Bottle / Lightning Perfume Bottle / Chilling Perfume Bottle / Frenzyflame Perfume Bottle / Deadly Poison Perfume Bottle
    • Increased attack power.
  • Lordsworn's Shield / Briar Greatshield / Spiked Palisade Shield / Icon Shield / Golden Beast Crest Shield / Manor Towershield / Crossed-Tree Towershield / Inverted Hawk Towershield / Dragon Towershield / Distinguished Greatshield / Gilded Greatshield / Black Steel Greatshield / Ant's Skull Plate / Erdtree Greatshield
    • Increased guard boost.
    • Reduced weight.
  • Wooden Greatshield / Cuckoo Greatshield / Redmane Greatshield / Golden Greatshield / Crucible Hornshield / Dragonclaw Shield / Eclipse Crest Greatshield / Jellyfish Shield / One-Eyed Shield
    • Increased guard boost.
  • Haligtree Crest Greatshield
    • Reduced weight.
  • Rakshasa's Great Katana
    • Increased the time before an attack can be performed with a right-hand weapon immediately after attacking with this weapon equipped in the left hand.
Skills
  • Parry
    • Improved parry performance.
    • Reduced the time before various actions can be performed after activation when used with Daggers, Curved Swords, or Small Shields.
  • Storm Wall
    • Changed the skill so that it no longer consumes FP when used.
    • Improved parry performance.
  • Thops's Barrier
    • Improved parry performance.
Sorceries
  • Founding Rain of Stars
    • Increased power.
  • Carian Retaliation
    • Increased power.
  • Meteorite
    • Reduced casting time.
  • Meteorite of Astel
    • Reduced casting time.
  • Gravitational Missile
    • Changed the spell so that the gravity projectile does not explode immediately upon striking terrain such as the ground or a wall.
Incantations
  • Feather of the Divine Bird
    • Increased power.
  • O, Flame!
    • Expanded attack range.
  • Rain of Fire
    • Increased power.

PvP-Exclusive Balance Adjustments

Weapons
  • Rakshasa's Great Katana
    • Increased damage taken from attacks by other players while attacking.
Incantations
  • Rugalea's Roar
    • Reduced power against other players.
  • Rotten Breath / Ekzykes's Decay
    • Reduced the amount of time other player characters are unable to move from hit reactions when struck by these incantations.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed a bug where critical hits dealt with Great Katana weapon types had lower-than-expected power against large enemies.
  • Fixed a bug where jumping attacks with Great Katana weapon types could be parried.

PC-Only Bug Fixes

  • Fixed a bug that prevented camera control with the mouse during NPC dialogue when using keyboard and mouse controls
  • Fixed a bug in the "Keyboard/Mouse Settings" section of the system menu in which selecting the reset option did not restore various settings to their defaults

The version number shown in the lower-right corner of the title screen after applying this update will be as follows:

App Ver. 1.17
Regulation Ver. 1.17

This update is required for online play.

We will continue to make improvements so that you can enjoy ELDEN RING more comfortably.

Thank you for your continued support.

items.title: Helldivers 2 Boss Happy That GTA 6 Is Skipping PC at Launch and There's No Online Right Away
items.description: Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that’s one of the reasons we have a September crush of video game releases. But according to the CEO of Helldivers 2 developer Arrowhead, there are two very good reasons why developers shouldn’t be too worried.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that’s one of the reasons we have a September crush of video game releases. But according to the CEO of Helldivers 2 developer Arrowhead, there are two very good reasons why developers shouldn’t be too worried.

Speaking to IGN, Arrowhead boss Shams Jorjani said that the lack of a PC version of GTA 6 at launch, as well as the absence of whatever the next generation of GTA Online looks like, means there’s reason to believe games like Helldivers 2 retain their own space.

“Rockstar makes ridiculous, high-effort stuff and it's awesome that games like this get made,” Jorjani said. “On a selfish level I'm happy it’s not hitting PC right away, and that online isn’t dropping at launch. It means Helldivers 2 gets to keep crushing it in our own space, and is also why it won’t be the all consuming behemoth everyone’s worried about.

“Everyone in the industry right now is constantly pivoting strategies and obsessing over early player feedback just to survive. But Rockstar has the brand power to confidently take their time and run their classic play. They have the confidence and freedom to spend a decade doing things the old-school way because they know the core game will deliver. It’s going to raise the bar for sure.”

Of course, Helldivers 2 is also out on console (it’s a PlayStation Studios game and Sony owns the Helldivers IP), but the explosive co-op action game is particularly strong on Steam, where it retains a loyal and sizeable audience of fans even now, two-and-a-half years after launch.

You’d image that the launch of GTA 6 will have an impact on even PC games, but perhaps long-running Steam games that revolve around online play will prove more resilient than others. Let's remember: GTA 6 is a single-player game at launch. There's no online mode at all this November.

GTA 6 is also set for launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S only, which in 2026 feels like an odd release strategy but is in keeping with Rockstar’s playbook. Jorjani touches on this in his comment — Rockstar is perhaps one of the few video game developers around that can guarantee success even skipping PC. GTA 6 is just that big of a deal. There’s nothing like it.

Be sure to check out IGN’s GTA 6 official gameplay reveal live blog, where we’ll bring you all the news across the internet on today’s Netflix exclusive and beyond.

items.title: Rockstar Games and Florida Officials Are Having Conversations to Turn Miami Into Vice City IRL for GTA 6's Marketing Campaign
items.description: Florida officials and Rockstar Games are having conversations to turn parts of Miami into Vice City for Grand Theft Auto 6's marketing campaign.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Florida officials and Rockstar Games are having conversations to turn parts of Miami into Vice City for Grand Theft Auto 6's marketing campaign.

As initially reported by The Miamian, Miami-Dade County has had formal conversations with Rockstar Games about a Grand Theft Auto 6-themed takeover of Miami to promote the upcoming game. The report initially noted that Rockstar was the one that approached Miami-Dade with its ideas, but the article was later edited to clarify the city was actually the one who submitted a pitch deck.

While no plans are officially in place yet, the ideas pitched by the city are wide-ranging, ambitious, and likely absurdly expensive. One such idea includes transforming a section of Miami International Airport to serve as a "welcome" area for Vice City, complete with Vice City signage, limited edition luggage tags, themed luggage carts, a photo backdrop, and even a display aircraft wrapped in the game's purple color scheme.

Officials also proposed various activations around Miami's beaches, parks, and ports, creating unique events with DJs, food, exotic vehicles, photo ops, drone shows, murals, and much more. Outside of actual events, there are even ideas to have Rockstar take over the city's busses and trains with Vice City branding on the actual locomotives and stations associated with them. On the smaller side, there was also a pitch for Vice City-branded manhole covers and utility boxes.

The city created a number of proposals that would actually permanently help Miami in the long term, such as the creation of more bus shelters, quality of life improvements for its parks, and more. One of the more unique suggestions included the construction of a "radio lab" at a library in downton Miami. This would give visitors access to recording and editing equipment to produce music, podcasts, and more.

In a statement to The Miamian, Carlos Suarez, a spokesperson for Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava, confirmed that they've had conversations with Rockstar Games, but there are no concrete plans in place at the moment.

“Nothing has been formally agreed to or approved, and any idea would have to go through the appropriate review and approval process," said Suarez. "Given Miami-Dade's clear influence on the game, we think there could be a unique opportunity to generate revenue for the County while showcasing Miami-Dade to a massive audience.”

It wouldn't be surprising if Rockstar uses the city of Miami to promote GTA 6 as part of its expansive marketing campaign, but it seems unlikely that it would go forth with all of these ideas. Not only are they expensive, but they may not all make sense for what Rockstar is envisioning for its advertising campaign.

The final marketing push for GTA 6 will ramp up today when Rockstar premieres an extended look at the game on Netflix. If you don't have Netflix or simply don't have time to watch, IGN will be doing a live blog with all of the big news from Rockstar's reveal. Additionally, a few new details were revealed yesterday including tidbits about specific gameplay mechanics and Rockstar doubling its size in order to produce GTA 6.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: State of Decay 3 Announces Closed Beta Playtests Later This Year
items.description: State of Decay 3 fans will have the chance to play the game later this year via a closed beta.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
State of Decay 3 fans will have the chance to play the game later this year via a closed beta.

Undead Labs has confirmed that it will hold a closed beta for State of Decay 3 before the end of 2026. Exact dates weren't given, but interested fans can sign up now by clicking here and filling out the required information. The studio also held an alpha earlier this year, which reportedly resulted in actionable feedback to improve the game. The team noted that the alpha allowed them to improve combat, cosmetics, visuals, and movement, resulting in a better product. The beta will only allow more opportunities to improve the game, according to Undead Labs.

“We’re going to be expanding our alpha and then closed beta to more players over time, this is our largest map ever and with untethered multiplayer, we really need to take the opportunities to stress-test and fine-tune,” said Kevin Patzelt, Creative Director at Undead Labs. “If you don’t get access right away, rest assured there will be more opportunities throughout the year for players familiar and brand new to the series.”

State of Decay 3 has been in the works since at least 2020, when the game was announced at the Xbox Series X/S reveal event. The project went quiet for a number of years, but was re-revealed in 2024 and is now planned for release sometime in 2027. It's been a long road, and it hasn't been an easy one. Undead Labs is also splitting away from Xbox, as part of the platform's big reset. Xbox underwent a massive restructuring earlier this summer, leading to extensive layoffs and multiple studios being sold off or released to go independent.

Undead Labs is in the process of transitioning out of Xbox, though it's currently unclear what the studio's new path is, such as acquisition by another company or forging its own path. Additionally, it has been reported that Undead Labs will not be obligated to bring State of Decay 3 to Xbox Game Pass once it leaves Xbox. However, the blog post announcing the closed beta noted that the game is still planned for a Game Pass release. So, I guess we'll just have to wait and see what happens.

State of Decay 3 will release on Xbox Series X/S, PS5, and PC next year.

items.title: GTA 6 Leaker Has 'Cashed Out' and Reportedly Earned Around $270,000, Fans Believe
items.description: Analysis of overnight cryptocurrency transactions points to the prolific GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out" of their meme coin, earning around $270,000 in the process.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Analysis of overnight cryptocurrency transactions points to the prolific GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out" of their meme coin, earning around $270,000 in the process.

That's according to reliable GTA watcher and crypto analyst Vice Cit, who previously posted evidence that strongly suggested the leaking antics of "Cyberleek" were part of a cryptocurrency scheme, rather than their claimed excuse of it being a protest against the death of physical media.

Every video posted by the person or persons known as Cyberleek has pointed to a website where fans could pay to vote on further leaks using the leaker's own cryptocurrency. These leaks have since increased in frequency over the past few days, and also escalated in terms of the content they showed — revealing full frontal nudity in one recent video, and then finally beginning to spoil the game's story in the latest clip posted to date.

The rapid release of more leaks, as well as Rockstar's own impending official reveal of gameplay footage via Netflix, suggested to some fans that Cyberleek was getting ready to make their move and earn whatever money they could before interest waned and their currency inevitably collapsed.

Indeed, this now appears to be the case, with Cyberleek apparently pocketing all the currency's trading fees and transferring them into at least two other sources overnight, ready for withdrawal. Vice Cit has a detailed log of where the money went, up to a point, but not enough to help identify who was actually behind it all. The fact that multiple withdrawal methods were allegedly used could point to multiple people being behind Cyberleek, Vice Cit speculated, though this cannot be confirmed.

Whether the culprit or culprits are ever caught now seems to rely on how successful Rockstar's legal team and the relevant law authorities are at forcing social networks or crypto exchanges to divulge any personal details they hold on those responsible.

"The original setup of this whole project (the CYBERLEEK token, the website, and the file uploads) was around $29,000 at the time of my first investigation," Vice Cit wrote. "Which means the person or group behind this leak profited around $241,000 if this is where this all ends. Not an amount to completely dismiss but is it really 'risk your freedom money'?

"I personally believe the leaker expected to make much more from this project and the watermark messaging in the most recent clips feels kind of panicky. As the coin continued to drop over the last 24 hours and the public started to lose interest I believe the leaker made the choice to cash out."

And then there's the million dollar (or $241,000) question: Are the GTA 6 leaks over? There's no reason why Cyberleek couldn't release more footage, and no suggestion they were close to getting caught. Indeed, it would be the ultimate test of Cyberleek actually caring about their stated cause of physical media if they continued posting even now. Time will tell, though at the time of writing Rockstar is now just hours from taking center stage.

Follow along with all of today's announcements in our Grand Theft Auto 6: Extended Look liveblog.

items.title: Toy Story 5 Is Coming to Disney+ Next Month
items.description: Toy Story 5, which is now the highest-grossing movie in the franchise, is officially coming to Disney+ on September 23.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Toy Story 5 is officially coming to Disney+ on September 23.

The streaming release date is just over four months after the film’s initial release in theaters, a standard timeline for Pixar movies. A spread of 4K Blu-rays, including a highly sought after 4K steelbook, will be released the day before, on September 22. The movie is also already available to rent or purchase digitally from PVOD platforms.

A new trailer was released in anticipation of the Disney+ arrival that largely features an army of Buzz Lightyears. The streaming release announcement is also accompanied by a new music video for the piano version of the Taylor Swift song featured in the movie, “I Knew It, I Knew You," now available on Spotify, Apple Music, and Disney+.

Toy Story 5 grossed just over $1.1 billion worldwide with a reported budget of $250 million, surpassing the box office performance of the previous sequel, Toy Story 4. The Toy Story franchise as a whole has now grossed over $3.3 billion, and only slightly trails behind Universal's Despicable Me as the second highest-grossing animated media franchise of all time.

The latest Pixar sequel introduces a new villain, LilyPad, tackling the topic of technology for kids. Following the end of Toy Story 4, Woody is a little less of a main character, with the movie instead focusing more on Jessie, Buzz, and a gaggle of new characters.

The movie currently sits at a 93% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, the lowest in the very acclaimed franchise. Critic Clint Gage gave the film a 7/10 in his review for IGN, saying it ultimately "manages to pull off an adventurous and resonant conclusion."

The sequel's box office success follows what Pixar reported as a disappointing run for Hoppers, which was in part blamed for recent layoffs at the studio. Still, Pixar will be going back to originals with its next movie, Gatto, slated for release next March. There’s been no official word on what’s next for the Toy Story saga, but the franchise does seem to always find its way back.

items.title: The Witcher 3 Price Quietly Increased Ahead of Remaster Release
items.description: The Witcher 3 has gotten a price increase ahead of the release of the game's remaster next month.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The Witcher 3 has gotten a price increase ahead of the release of the game's remaster next month.

Earlier this week, CD Projekt Red surprised fans by announcing a new remaster for The Witcher 3. It will feature visual enhancements, changes to combat, and much, much more. The best part? It's completely free to existing owners of The Witcher 3 and if you don't already own the DLCs, you're getting those for free. However, if you haven't bought the game, you will now have to pay a bit extra.

The price of The Witcher 3: Complete Edition on Steam has jumped from $39.99 to $49.99 since the announcement of the remaster. This will be the price of the remaster itself, so fans who buy the existing version are essentially paying for the new version upfront since their copy will be automatically upgraded. It's not a huge jump, but may be a bummer for those who have been waiting for the right opportunity to buy The Witcher 3 and now have to pay a bit more, especially since the game is 11 years old.

The Witcher 3 is arguably worth the price of admission, though. The game, with all of its DLCs and side quests, is hundreds of hours long and is highly replayable. items.title: Peter Cullen, Optimus Prime in Transformers, Dies at 85
items.description: Peter Cullen, the voice of Optimus Prime in Transformers and countless other roles, has died at 85.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Peter Cullen, the voice of Optimus Prime in Transformers and countless other roles, has died at 85.

The legendary TV and movie voice actor passed away at his home Wednesday, August 26, his family and agent confirmed to TMZ. Additional details regarding his death have not been announced at this time.

A Canada-born actor since the '60s with decades of voice and on-camera work, Cullen has a long history of bringing his strong-and-gentle talents to movies and TV, but his most famous work is easily his role as Autobot leader and Transformers hero Optimus Prime. The character has remained one of the prevailing fictional figures of the '80s, thanks in no small part to the part Cullen played in bringing him to life.

Cullen first played Optimus Prime for the original Transformers series and returned to bring his iconic delivery to the world of Cybertron in countless sequels, spinoffs, and adaptations in the decades that followed. You may have missed him in the first Transformers movie or the War for Cybertron video game that released in 2010, for example, but there's still a good chance you caught Cullen returning to the Autobots for live-action Transformers movies like 2023's Rise of the Beasts or 2017's The Last Knight.

Cullen was an icon in the voice acting world, and there's no question that his role as Optimus Prime will stand the test of time, but his credits extend far beyond a universe of transforming alien semi-trucks. The actor also notably brought his low-register delivery to Disney classics as Winnie the Pooh's pessimistic donkey friend, Eeyore. He also chipped into the Predator universe as its first Predator and even played a role in 1976's King Kong.

Knight Rider, Spider-Man, Voltron, My Little Pony, G.I. Joe, and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles; the list goes on. TV fans most recently would have caught him as Thaedus in Invincible, but his contributions to entertainment will not be forgotten anytime soon.

"Peter Cullen passed away peacefully, surrounded by his loving family — and held in the hearts of his many friends and countless fans worldwide," his family said in a statement. "His family asks that you honor his remarkable legacy by serving your communities and leading others with compassion, integrity, and loyalty and always remember 'be strong enough to be gentle.'"

Cullen's voice rings in the minds of fans everywhere, so it should come as no surprise to see many of his followers already taking to social media to share their favorite moments from his career. You can see how some are paying their respects below.

“Be Strong enough to be gentle.”

Peter Cullen tells the story of how his brother inspired the voice he would use to play Optimus Prime. It’s a simple yet poignant quote that sums up why Optimus and Peter are so beloved.

Peter Cullen used to cut promos for Toonami back in the day. The promo he did for Rurouni Kenshin got me so hype. pic.twitter.com/9BTFXCUGss

— 🤘🏾 (@newjack5000) August 27, 2026

rest in peace peter cullen
thank you for my childhood 🖤 pic.twitter.com/f1WefufA5k

— h. (@6ixImmortal) August 27, 2026

Optimus Prime: "Freedom is the right of all sentient beings."

Rest in Peace, Peter Cullen. pic.twitter.com/rUJ4H4Hz4l

— Blaze Binges (@BlazeBinges) August 27, 2026

Peter Cullen was the sole voice that was responsible for generating hype for anime coming to the west.

RIP Legend https://t.co/7pN2VgNXfr pic.twitter.com/YhYRY0Ne3t

— kate bush’s husband (@airbagg3d) August 27, 2026

"if I'm going out, I'm gonna go out big!"

Thanks for the memories, Peter Cullen! pic.twitter.com/gq1f7VFhmG

— crazy ass moments in Transformers history (@TF_Moments) August 27, 2026

I'm actually shaking and crying and I'm really not ok.

The only other time I've cried for someone passing was my dad, I don't know what to think right now.

This is a sad day for the fandom, I hope his family knows that he was a role model for millions upon millions of people. https://t.co/36iGfXS0V1

— TFHypeGuy (@TFHypeGuy) August 27, 2026

What a damned week.

I became friends with Peter a couple of years back. A prime example of a Canadian adventurer, storyteller, and a colossal, optimal talent.

No one better to chat over whiskies with.#LoveYouPeterCullen https://t.co/vjHodq11ix

items.title: Exclusive: The Lancer TTRPG Is Getting New Hardcover Editions in 2027
items.author: Jacob Kienlen
items.content:
Massif Press and Dark Horse Books are releasing two new printed editions for the Lancer TTRPG next year. Operation Fulcrum Dawn: Introductory Narrative Modules for Lancer and Lancer: Setting Guide Volume 1 are both set to release in March 2027 with preorders starting today.

The new books are meant to be paired with the core rulebook, which first launched in 2024. Check out the images and descriptions below to get a first look of what to expect:

Operation Fulcrum Dawn: Introductory Narrative Modules for Lancer

The upcoming book collects two new modules meant to introduce new players to the game. Here are the official descriptions of each module:

Operation Solstice Rain takes characters from License Level (LL) 0 to LL 2 across two missions of pitched urban combat in the city of Nov Elysia. As a squad of rookie Union mech pilots, the player characters (PCs) undertake a rescue operation amidst a burgeoning conflict between the Leandric States Alliance and the Vestan Sovereignty. Though this may be their first time in combat, they’ll need to use every bit of their training and push their mechs to the limit if they want to survive!

Operation Winter Scar guides characters all the way to LL 4 across two more missions, pitting the now-seasoned pilots against the Vestan Sovereignty Armed Forces. From advanced combat chassis to main battle tanks, the Sovereignty will stop at nothing in their efforts to push the pilots back!

Where to buy

The hardcover edition also includes printed battle maps and tactical advice for those not already familiar with the gameplay. Preorders will be going live today at Dark Horse Direct, Amazon, Barnes and Noble, and other online bookstores for $29.99 with a release date of March 16, 2027.

Lancer: Setting Guide Volume 1

The upcoming settings guide features two settings expansions collected into one book. Here are the official descriptions of each:

Touch down in the Karrakin Trade Barronies, the oldest human civilization in Union space. A place of deep tradition and legend, the Baronies is increasingly a realm of surging political intrigue and social division! But the great engine of industry in the Baronies is grinding to a halt, and a rising tide of Republicanism threatens to shake the Baronies to its core. Will you help usher in a new age for old Karrakis, or stand aside lest you be crushed?

And set your sights on the Long Rim, a lawless sector of Union space. It is home to corrupt, self-serving Enterprises; pirate outfits that prey on unprotected ships; and myriad other groups, from the uncanny HORUS cells to the clandestine Horizon Collective. Alone, or with your small squad, you can't change the Rim; but you can make your mark, whether as a scoundrel or paragon.

Where to buy

Preorders for the first setting guide will be going live today at Dark Horse Direct, Amazon, Barnes and Noble, and other online bookstores with a March 30, 2027 release date. This book will also be priced at $29.99

items.title: LIVE: Rockstar Finally Reveals Official GTA 6 Gameplay, First on Netflix
items.description: Today is the day Rockstar Games finally pulls back the curtain on the most anticipated video game of all time: Grand Theft Auto 6 — and IGN is reporting live with all the news from across the internet.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
GTA 6 REVEAL SUMMARY

  • We visited Rockstar North to see GTA 6 and came away seriously impressed by a live gameplay demo. The 30-minute play session showcased a Grand Theft Auto with a huge emphasis on the little details that make an open world feel like a real place.
  • We spoke to Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North, to learn about how GTA 6 is building on the series’ almost 30-year legacy: “It’s a Step Forward in All Respects.”
  • Across both the new “Extended Look” video and the demo session we saw at Rockstar, we’ve learned many new gameplay details.
  • GTA 6 will feature ‘a Very Big Map’ that’s home to its most complex world yet.
  • That world features the same style of satirical humour GTA is historically known for, but Rockstar admits it has to be “careful” with its jokes.
  • The developer considered four protagonists for GTA 6 before settling on a criminal couple.
  • Jason and Lucia’s Bonnie and Clyde-style romance is optional, and can be played more like a platonic partnership.
  • With over a decade of anticipation, Rockstar is “nervous” about the pressure to deliver.

Today is the day Rockstar Games finally pulls back the curtain on the most anticipated video game of all time: Grand Theft Auto 6 — and IGN is reporting live with all the news from across the internet.

GTA 6 was confirmed four-and-a-half years ago, when Rockstar said work on the next game in the phenomenally successful franchise was in development. Following two trailers and two public delays, we are now about to get an official gameplay reveal. Netflix goes first with its Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look, which remains exclusive to the streaming platform for six hours. Netflix has said this reveal was captured entirely from in-game footage on PlayStation 5, and runs 27 minutes.

Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look Netflix and YouTube global release times:

  • 5am Friday, August 28 (Netflix)
  • 11am Friday, August 28 (YouTube)

  • 4am Friday, August 28 (Netflix)
  • 10am Friday, August 28 (YouTube)

  • 4am Friday, August 28 (Netflix)
  • 10am Friday, August 28 (YouTube)

  • 3am Friday, August 28 (Netflix)
  • 9am Friday, August 28 (YouTube)

  • 11pm Thursday, August 27 (Netflix)
  • 5am Friday, August 28 (YouTube)

  • 9pm Thursday, August 27 (Netflix)
  • 3am Friday, August 28 (YouTube)

  • 9pm Thursday, August 27 (Netflix)
  • 3am Friday, August 28 (YouTube)

  • 8pm Thursday, August 27 (Netflix)
  • 2am Friday, August 28 (YouTube)

  • 4pm Thursday, August 27 (Netflix)
  • 10pm Thursday, August 27 (YouTube)

  • 3pm Thursday, August 27 (Netflix)
  • 9pm Thursday, August 27 (YouTube)

PDT (Los Angeles):

  • 12pm Thursday, August 27 (Netflix)
  • 6pm Thursday, August 27 (YouTube)

In the run up to today’s reveal, Rockstar has suffered a long list of gameplay leaks, which it responded to earlier this week. But enthusiasm for GTA 6 continues ahead of its November 19, 2026 release, and we’ll have all the news as it happens throughout the day, including the Netflix reveal itself and beyond.

So check out our live reporting below as the action unfolds. You won’t want to miss this one!

GTA 6 is revealed!

The GTA 6 gameplay is now live on Netflix, and IGN has loads of fresh exclusive content on the game. We've got new screenshots, below, including one exclusive to IGN.

30 minutes to go!

Only 30 minutes remain before the GTA 6 gameplay reveal on Netflix. Not long now!

Rockstar and Florida Officials Are Reportedly Talking About Turning Miami Into Vice City IRL for GTA 6 Marketing Campaign

Florida officials and Rockstar Games are having conversations to turn parts of Miami into Vice City for GTA 6's marketing campaign. As initially reported by The Miamian, Miami-Dade County has had formal conversations with Rockstar about a GTA 6-themed takeover of Miami to promote the upcoming game. More here.

Helldivers 2 Boss Happy That GTA 6 Is Skipping PC at Launch and There's No Online Right Away

Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that’s one of the reasons we have a September crush of video game releases. But according to the CEO of Helldivers 2 developer Arrowhead, there are two very good reasons why developers shouldn’t be too worried. More here.

GTA 6 Leaker Has 'Cashed Out'

Analysis of overnight cryptocurrency transactions points to the prolific GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out" of their meme coin, earning around $270,000 in the process. More here.

Let's remember GTA 6 Trailer 2

Rockstar then released GTA 6 Trailer 2 in May 2025, a year-and-a-half after Trailer 1. Anticipation was fever pitch at this point, with fans going down increasingly elaborate rabbit holes in their bid for new details and release date. The release of Trailer 2 came hot on the heels of a delay to GTA 6 itself, from fall 2025 to May 2026 (it would go on to be delayed again, to November 19, 2026).

GTA 6 Trailer 2 was captured on base PS5, as today's reveal is. "Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them," Rockstar said in the official description released at the time. "But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive."

If you need a refresh, Trailer 2 is below:

Let's remember GTA 6 Trailer 1

Rockstar formally announced GTA 6 in December 2023 with the release of Trailer 1. The developer confirmed the Trailer 1 launch window a month prior, issuing a rare statement from Rockstar co-founder Sam Houser:

Next month marks the 25th anniversary of Rockstar Games.
Thanks to the incredible support of our players worldwide, we have had the opportunity to create games we are truly passionate about — without you, none of this would be possible, and we are so grateful to all of you for sharing this journey with us.
In 1998, Rockstar Games was founded on the idea that video games could come to be as essential to culture as any other form of entertainment, and we hope that we have created games you love in our efforts to be part of that evolution.
We are very excited to let you know that in early December, we will release the first trailer for the next Grand Theft Auto.
We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with all of you.
Thank you,
Sam Houser

In the end, Rockstar was forced to release GTA 6 Trailer 1 early due to a leak (GTA 6 and leaks have a long history). If you're struggling to remember what was in it, check out Trailer 1 below.

Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have RPG Mechanics Like Eating, Exercising, and More

Ahead of the Netflix reveal, a cover story for Dazed magazine, revealed new information about GTA 6, which we've rounded up here. Highlights include players being able to eat, work out, and sleep, each of which has an impact on the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

As initially reported by The Miamian, Miami-Dade County has had formal conversations with Rockstar about a GTA 6-themed takeover of Miami to promote the upcoming game. More here.

Helldivers 2 Boss Happy That GTA 6 Is Skipping PC at Launch and There's No Online Right Away

Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that’s one of the reasons we have a September crush of video game releases. But according to the CEO of Helldivers 2 developer Arrowhead, there are two very good reasons why developers shouldn’t be too worried. More here.

GTA 6 Leaker Has 'Cashed Out'

Analysis of overnight cryptocurrency transactions points to the prolific GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out" of their meme coin, earning around $270,000 in the process. More here.

Let's remember GTA 6 Trailer 2

Rockstar then released GTA 6 Trailer 2 in May 2025, a year-and-a-half after Trailer 1. Anticipation was fever pitch at this point, with fans going down increasingly elaborate rabbit holes in their bid for new details and release date. The release of Trailer 2 came hot on the heels of a delay to GTA 6 itself, from fall 2025 to May 2026 (it would go on to be delayed again, to November 19, 2026).

GTA 6 Trailer 2 was captured on base PS5, as today's reveal is. "Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them," Rockstar said in the official description released at the time. "But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive."

If you need a refresh, Trailer 2 is below:

Let's remember GTA 6 Trailer 1

Rockstar formally announced GTA 6 in December 2023 with the release of Trailer 1. The developer confirmed the Trailer 1 launch window a month prior, issuing a rare statement from Rockstar co-founder Sam Houser:

Next month marks the 25th anniversary of Rockstar Games.
Thanks to the incredible support of our players worldwide, we have had the opportunity to create games we are truly passionate about — without you, none of this would be possible, and we are so grateful to all of you for sharing this journey with us.
In 1998, Rockstar Games was founded on the idea that video games could come to be as essential to culture as any other form of entertainment, and we hope that we have created games you love in our efforts to be part of that evolution.
We are very excited to let you know that in early December, we will release the first trailer for the next Grand Theft Auto.
We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with all of you.
Thank you,
Sam Houser

In the end, Rockstar was forced to release GTA 6 Trailer 1 early due to a leak (GTA 6 and leaks have a long history). If you're struggling to remember what was in it, check out Trailer 1 below.

Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have RPG Mechanics Like Eating, Exercising, and More

Ahead of the Netflix reveal, a cover story for Dazed magazine, revealed new information about GTA 6, which we've rounded up here. Highlights include players being able to eat, work out, and sleep, each of which has an impact on the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia.

items.title: Fable Was Previously Aiming for an October Launch, Director Reveals, Insisting That the Game's Delay Wasn't Due to Being 'Scared of Other Big Games'
items.description: Fable is set to release on February 23, 2027, and developer Playground Games is feeling pretty confident that it will be ready for that date.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Fable is set to release on February 23, 2027, and developer Playground Games is feeling pretty confident that it will be ready for that date.

Speaking to IGN at gamescom, the RPG’s director, Ralph Fulton, told us that he feels “great about it.”

“I think the rationale behind moving us out of October, the date that we were in previously, is pretty apparent to everybody,” he continues. “I feel great about that. I mean, I was really looking forward to shipping this game this year. I didn't want to have to do another January 1st speech to the team about ‘this is the year we ship Fable,’ which I'm now going to have to do. But the rationale for it is absolutely sound. I'm glad that we're avoiding that chaotic window.”

This is actually the first we’ve officially heard about the game having previously been earmarked for an October 2026. Prior to the announcement of the February date, we had only been given a window of "this fall.”

It makes sense that Playground’s reimagining of the formerly Microsoft-exclusive series decided to move out of October. Fulton isn’t wrong about it being a chaotic time of year with another Xbox Games Studio release, Gears of War E-Day coming that month, along with the likes of PS5 console exclusive, Phantom Blade Zero.

Those games are sandwiched between a packed September involving the likes of Marvel’s Wolverine, Control Resonant, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and Silent Hill: Townfall to name but a few. That doesn’t mean February of next year is looking any clearer, though, with many other game developers seemingly having had a similar idea to Fable. Indeed, Playground's RPG will launch against God of War Laufey, Metro 2039, and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

Fulton isn’t worried about the beginning of next year suddenly looking like another busy period for big games releases, however. “People keep saying that to me, but we don't run scared of other big games,” says Fulton.

“We're a big game ourselves. We hold ourselves to high standards. I'm happy to go toe-to-toe with a bunch of other games. There's just one that I'm happy to avoid entirely.”

That game is, of course, GTA 6. Stay tuned tonight for more on Rockstar’s upcoming return to Vice City, where we’ll have plenty of reaction and insight alongside the Extended Look debuting on Netflix.

For more Fable, check out our gamescom previews where we’ve got impressions of a full quest, plus our thoughts on how its combat is shaping up after playing.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look Runtime Revealed, Features Footage Captured on PS5
items.description: Netflix has revealed the runtime of today's Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look broadcast, and confirmed it will feature footage captured on PlayStation 5.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Netflix has revealed the runtime of today's Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look broadcast, and confirmed it will feature footage captured on PlayStation 5.

Today brings our first (official) look at Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay, in a lengthy deep dive into the game that has become overshadowed somewhat by the past week's string of unprecedented leaks.

Regardless, developer Rockstar is pushing on with its own reveal plans, including today's unique timed-exclusive for Netflix. Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look will run for 27 minutes, the streaming service has now confirmed, and debut PS5 gameplay.

"Captured entirely from in-game footage on PlayStation 5, this extended look at the next Grand Theft Auto showcases the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet," a Netflix blog post states.

The fact we're specifically going to see the PS5 version of GTA 6 is not a surprise. Sony and PlayStation have already demonstrated they have secured a strong marketing partnership with Rockstar for the game, via high-profile ads on the PS5 itself, and messages telling PS4 owners they'll need to upgrade their console to play the upcoming blockbuster. The two companies have also stated that GTA 5 will "run best" on PS5, presumably on the higher-powered PS5 Pro.

At the time of writing, just a few hours remain to the Extended Look's reveal later today on Netflix, and then its wider released elsewhere (such as YouTube) six hours later. IGN will have extensive coverage of everything revealed about GTA 6 today, and will be reporting live as the afternoon and evening unfold. For a comprehensive guide to when Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look debuts both on Netflix and later on YouTube in your timezone, IGN has you covered.

Outside of that, one deep-dive article on the game published already has revealed a slew of gameplay details, such as how eating, exercising and partying will impact your character's physical appearance. We also now know that Rockstar doubled its team size to complete the game.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social
